justifications.fr: Le monastère de Guadalupe conserve un plafond semblable à l’exemplaire cordouan.
justifications.es: El monasterio de Guadalupe conserva un alfarje parecido al ejemplar cordobés.

justifications.ar: دعامات  خشبية كبيرة تحمل أسقف مسجد القيروان مثل سقف قرطبة.
justifications.en: Large wooden beams held up the ceilings of the Kairouan Mosque, like the Córdoban ceiling.
justifications.fr: De grandes poutres de bois soutiennent les plafonds de la mosquée de Kairouan, comme pour le plafond cordouan.
justifications.es: Grandes vigas de madera sustentan las techumbres de la mezquita de Qayrawan, como en el alfarje cordobés.

justifications.ar: هذا الإفريز الخشبي المريني معاصر للسقف المدجن.
justifications.en: This wooden Marinid frieze is contemporary to the Mudejar ceiling.
justifications.fr: Cette frise de bois mérinide est contemporaine du plafond mudéjar.
justifications.es: Este friso de madera meriní es contemporáneo del alfarje mudéjar.

justifications.ar: هذا الجزء من الدعامة  أيضا مرسوم عليه رسوم نباتات و هو سابق للجوائز من السقف القرطبي.
justifications.en: This beam fragment, also painted with plant motifs, is an antecedent of the beams from the Córdoban ceiling.
justifications.fr: Ce fragment de poutre, également peint avec des motifs végétaux, est un précédent des poutres du plafond cordouan.
justifications.es: Este fragmento de viga, pintado también con motivos vegetales, es un antecedente de las vigas del alfarje cordobés.

justifications.ar: إن تزيينه و نقوشه تبين أن هذا الصحن المقعر (الطيفور) هو جزء من معدات الطبخ في مدينة الزهراء.
justifications.en: Its decoration and inscription suggest that this *ataifor* may have been part of the crockery at Madinat al-Zahra.
justifications.fr: Par le type de décoration et l’épigraphe, cet ataifor a pu appartenir à la vaisselle palatine de Madinat al-Zahra.
justifications.es: El ataifor pudo pertenecer a la vajilla palatina de Madinat al-Zahra por el tipo de decoración y la inscripción.

justifications.ar: يتضمن هذا الوعاء أيضا النقش العربي لكلمة  الملك ( السلطة ).
justifications.en: This bowl also includes the inscription *al-mulk* (‘the power’).
justifications.fr: Sur cet ataifor se lit de nouveau le terme arabe al-moulk, “le pouvoir”.
justifications.es: En este ataifor aparece de nuevo el término árabe *al-mulk* (“el poder”).

justifications.ar: هذا الوعاء البرتغالي مزين باستخدام نفس التقنية التي تعرف بالأخضر و المنغنيز.
justifications.en: This Portuguese bowl is decorated using the same technique, known as ‘green and manganese’.
justifications.fr: Cet ataifor portugais était décoré avec la même technique appelée “vert et manganèse”.
justifications.es: Este ataifor portugués se decoró con la misma técnica, llamada “verde y manganeso”.

justifications.ar: يُعتقد أن الخزف العباسي المزين باللونين الأخضر والأرجواني على خلفية بيضاء هو سابقة لخزف قرطبة في عصر الخلافة.
justifications.en: Abbasid ceramics decorated in green and purple on a white background are though to be the antecedents of the ceramics of the Caliphate of Córdoba.
justifications.fr: La céramique abbasside décorée en vert et violet sur fond blanc est considérée comme un précédent de la céramique califale de Cordoue.
justifications.es: La cerámica abbasí decorada en color verde y morado sobre fondo blanco se considera antecedente de la califal cordobesa.

justifications.ar: أشجار النخيل بشكل مروحة التي تزين علبة المجوهرات هذه مشابهة للتي تظهر على حافة خزف الطيفور.
justifications.en: The fan-shaped palms that decorate this casket are similar to the ones that appear on the edge of the *ataifor*.
justifications.fr: Le type de palme digitée qui décore ce coffret califal est semblable à celui qui apparaît sur le rebord de l’ataifor.
justifications.es: El tipo de palma digitada que decora esta arqueta califal es similar al que aparece en el borde del ataifor.

justifications.ar: شهد الرحالة ابن جبير للمرور الآمن لقوافل التجارة للفرنجة و المسلمين حتى أثناء حصار صلاح الدين للكرك.
justifications.en: The traveller Ibn Jubayr witnessed the unhindered safe-passage of Frankish and Muslim trade caravans, even while Saladin held Karak under siege.
justifications.fr: Le voyageur Ibn Jubayr assista au passage, en toute tranquillité, des caravanes de commerce musulmanes et franques, alors même que Saladin tenait Karak en état de siège.
justifications.es: El viajero Ibn Jubayr presenció la circulación segura sin obstáculos de caravanas comerciales francas y musulmanes, incluso cuando Saladino mantuvo Al Karak bajo asedio.

justifications.ar: المحراب في المسجد الأقصى المقدس الذي أمر ببنائه  صلاح الدين يعود لنفس العام  الذي تم فيه الاحتفال بتحرير القدس.
justifications.en: The mihrab in the venerated al-Aqsa Mosque was commissioned by Saladin in the same year, celebrating the liberation of Jerusalem.
justifications.fr: Le mihrab de la très vénérée mosquée al-Aqsa fut commandité par Saladin la même année pour célébrer la libération de Jérusalem.
justifications.es: El mihrab en la venerada mezquita de al-Aqsa fue encargado por Saladino en el mismo año, para la celebración de la liberación de Jerusalén.

justifications.ar: نفس الحاكم الأيوبي الذي صك هذه القطعة النقدية أيضا رمم المسجد الأموي الكبير كما تذكِّر بذلك هذه اللوحة الرخامية.
justifications.en: Saladin completed the refurbishment of the marble panelling in the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus a year after this dinar issue was minted.
justifications.fr: Saladin acheva la remise à neuf du lambris de marbre dans la Grande Mosquée omeyyade de Damas un an après que ce dinar fut frappé.
justifications.es: Saladino completó la remodelación del revestimiento de mármol de la Gran Mezquita Omeya de Damasco un año después de que se acuñara este dinar.

justifications.ar: بالإضافة لصك النقد بنى صلاح الدين خانات  مثل الحصون لضمان استمرار التجارة و السفر.
justifications.en: In addition to minting coins, Saladin constructed fortress-like caravanserais to ensure the continuity of commerce and travel.
justifications.fr: En plus de frapper de la monnaie, Saladin fit construire des caravansérails ressemblant à des forteresses pour assurer la pérennité des transports et du commerce.
justifications.es: Además de acuñar las monedas, Saladino construyó caravasares como recintos amurallados para garantizar la continuidad del comercio y los viajes.

justifications.ar: هذا مثال عن نمط أولي فاطمي الذي تعتمد عليه القطع النقدية الأيوبية.
justifications.en: This is an example of the Fatimid prototype on which the Ayyubid coin is based.
justifications.fr: Ceci est un exemple du prototype fatimide sur lequel la pièce ayyoubide est basée.
justifications.es: Este es un ejemplo de un prototipo fatimí en el que se basa esta moneda ayubí.

justifications.ar: على خلاف القطع النقدية في شرق المتوسط فإن التصميم ذو الشكل المربع أدخل في الغرب خلال القرن السابع / الثالث عشر.
justifications.en: Unlike the coins in the eastern Mediterranean, a square shaped design was introduced in the west during the 7th/13th century.
justifications.fr: À la différence des pièces de monnaie de la Méditerranée orientale, un modèle de forme carrée fut introduit en Occident au cours du VIIe siècle H (XIIIe siècle J.-C.).
justifications.es: A diferencia de las monedas en el Mediterráneo oriental, un diseño cuadrado se introdujo en el oeste durante los siglos VII/ XIII.

justifications.en: The same Ayyubid ruler who minted this coin, Saladin, also restored the Great Umayyad Mosque, as commemorated by this marble panel.
justifications.fr: Le même souverain ayyoubide qui fit frapper cette pièce, Saladin, restaura également la Grande Mosquée omeyyade, ainsi que le commémore ce panneau de marbre.
justifications.es: El mismo gobernador ayubí que acuñó esta moneda, Saladino, también restauró la Gran Mezquita Omeya, como conmemora este panel de mármol.

justifications.ar: هذه القطع النقدية مشابهة لقطع صلاح الدين ولكنها ضربت بعد ذلك بنحو سبعين عاما و القطع النقدية الصليبية الجديدة ضربت في عام 649/1251 و تتجنب ذكر الأسماء أو العبارات الإسلامية.
justifications.en: Similar to Saladin’s coinage but minted some 70 years later, the new Crusader coins were struck in 649/1251 and avoid mention of Islamic names or phrases.
justifications.fr: Semblable à la monnaie de Saladin mais frappée quelque 70 ans plus tard, les nouvelles pièces franques furent frappées en 649 H / 1251 J.-C. et évitent de mentionner des noms ou phrases islamiques.
justifications.es: Parecidas a las monedas de Saladino, pero acuñadas alrededor de 70 años más tarde, las nuevas monedas de los cruzados fueron acuñadas en el 649/1251 y evitan mencionar nombres o frases islámicas.

justifications.ar: شهد الرحالة ابن جبير للمرور الآمن لقوافل التجارة للفرنجة و المسلمين حتى أثناء حصار صلاح الدين للكرك.
justifications.en: The traveller Ibn Jubayr witnessed the unhindered safe-passage of both Frankish and Muslim trade caravans, even while Saladin held Karak under siege.
justifications.fr: Le voyageur Ibn Jubayr assista au passage, en toute tranquillité, des caravanes de commerce musulmanes et franques, alors même que Saladin tenait Karak en état de siège.
justifications.es: El viajero Ibn Jubayr presenció la circulación segura sin obstáculos de caravanas comerciales francas y musulmanes, incluso cuando Saladino mantuvo Al Karak bajo asedio.

justifications.ar: هذا مثال عن نموذج أولي فاطمي يستخدم عادة في منطقة بلاد الشام( مصر ، فلسطين و سوريا ) خلال الحملات الصليبية.
justifications.en: This is an example of the Fatimid prototype commonly used in the region of the Levant (Egypt, Palestine and Syria) during the Crusades.
justifications.fr: Cette pièce d’or est un exemple du prototype fatimide couramment utilisé dans la région du Levant (Égypte, Palestine et Syrie) durant les Croisades.
justifications.es: Este es un ejemplo del prototipo fatimí utilizado comúnmente en la región del levante Mediterráneo (Egipto, Palestina y Siria) durante Las Cruzadas.

justifications.ar: هذه القطع النقدية الصليبية صكت بعد نحو سبعين عاما من إصدار صلاح الدين للدينار.
justifications.en: These Crusader coins were minted some 70 years after Saladin issued the dinar.
justifications.fr: Ces pièces franques ont été frappées quelque soixante-dix ans après que Saladin eut émis le dinar.
justifications.es: Estas monedas de Las Cruzadas fueron acuñadas alrededor de 70 años después de que Saladino expidiera el dinar.

justifications.ar: سكن القصر من قبل المنصور و من خلفه بمن فيهم الحاكم الذي صك هذه القطعة النقدية.
justifications.en: The palace was inhabited by al-Mansur and his successors, including the ruler who had this coin minted.
justifications.fr: Le Badii était le palais habité par al-Mansour et ses successeurs, dont le monarque qui a frappé la monnaie.
justifications.es: Al-Mansur y sus sucesores habitaban el palacio, incluso el gobernante que mandó a acuñar esta moneda.

justifications.ar: كانت المقبرة الملاذ الأخير للمنصور و من خلفه بمن فيهم الحاكم الذي صك هذه القطعة النقدية.
justifications.en: The necropolis was final resting place of al-Mansur and his successors, including the ruler who had the coin minted.
justifications.fr: La nécropole a servi de sépulture à Mansour al-Dahbi et à ses descendants.
justifications.es: La necrópolis fue el lugar de descanso final de al-Mansur y sus sucesores, incluido el gobernante que mandó a acuñar esta moneda.

justifications.ar: هذا الضريح هو قبر الملك مولاي  إدريس الثاني الذي قام بصك هذه القطعة النقدية.
justifications.en: This mausoleum is the tomb of King Mulay Idris II, who had this coin minted.
justifications.fr: Ce mausolée est le lieu de sépulture du monarque Moulay Idriss II qui a émis cette monnaie.
justifications.es: Este mausoleo es la tumba del rey Mulay Idris II quien acuñó esta moneda.

captions.ar: يُصوِّر الوجه الأمامي للتجليد حاكمًا شابًا يمتطي حصانًا ومحاطًا بحراسه. ويظهر أربعة من الرجال في أعلى المشهد وهم يمتطون الخيل، بينما يرافق الحاكمَ سيرًا على الأقدام الرجالُ الأقرب إليه مباشرة. ويتقدّم الجميع عبر حقلٍ مليء بالأزهار والنباتات الملوّنة. وتشير دوروثيا دودا إلى أن طريقة تصوير الحاكم تحمل تشابهًا واضحًا مع البورتريهات المعروفة للسلطان سليم الأول، وهو ما يعزّز الفرضية القائلة بأن هذا التجليد قد صُنع داخل الإمبراطورية العثمانية.
captions.en: The front of the binding depicts a young ruler riding on a horse surrounded by his guards. Four of the men on the top of the painting are also riding on horses, while the men directly next to the ruler are accompanying him by foot. The men are making their way through a field of colourful flowers and plants. Dorothea Duda points out that the way in which the ruler has been depicted bears a strong resemblance to known portraits of Sultan Selim I., which gives credence to the theory that this binding was manufactured within the Ottoman empire.

captions.ar: يعلى الغلاف الخلفي للتجليد نشاهد احتفالًا بلاطيًا. وفي وسط المشهد يجلس حاكم، تشير دوروثيا دودا مرة أخرى إلى أنه قد يكون تصويرًا آخر للسلطان سليم الأول، على عرشه الذهبي. ويحيط به عدد من الرجال يُرجَّح أنهم من أفراد بلاطه. ويجري هذا الاحتفال في فضاء خارجي مشابه للمشهد المصوَّر على الغلاف الأمامي للتجليد.
captions.en: On the back of the binding we see a courtly festivity taking place. In the centre of the scene a ruler, who Duda once again suggests could be another portrait of Sultan Selim I, sits upon his golden throne. He is surrounded by groups of men who are most likely members of his court. The festivity is taking place in an outdoor setting similar to the one on the front cover of the binding.

captions.ar: يُفتتح هذا الديوان بصفحة افتتاحية تمتد على صفحتين، تُصوِّر مشهد صيد نابضًا بالحركة لشبّان يمتطون الخيل، يرافقهم خدمهم سيرًا على الأقدام. في الصفحة 1b يظهر رجلان مع خدمهما في رحلة صيد داخل مرج أخضر، تعلوه الجبال في الخلفية. ويقفز حصان الشخصية المركزية في لحظة ديناميكية، بينما يقوم فارسه في الوقت نفسه بقتل غزال بسيفه. ويرتدي كلا الرجلين عمائم وملابس مزخرفة بدقة. أمّا الرجل الثاني، فيتميّز بلحية واضحة تشبّهها دوروثيا دودا بلحية السلطان سليمان القانوني. وتشير إضافة هذا البورتريه إلى احتمال أن تكون المخطوطة قد أُنجزت خلال فترة حكم السلطان سليم الأول.
captions.en:
This *divan* opens with a frontispiece spanning over two pages, depicting an energetic hunting scene with young men riding horses accompanied by their walking servants.  
On fol. 1b two men and their servants are on a hunt in a green meadow, behind which mountains loom. The horse of the central figure is making a leap whilst simultaneously its rider is slaying a gazelle with his sword. Both of the men are wearing turbans and intricately decorated clothing. The second man has a distinct beard that Dorothea Duda likens to the one Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent had. The inclusion of such a portrait indicates that the manuscript could have been finished during the reign of Sultan Selim I.

captions.ar: يعكس مشهد الصيد في الصفحة 2a المشهدَ المصوَّر في الصفحة 1b. يظهر رجلان يمتطيان الخيل في خضمّ الصيد ضمن منظر طبيعي مشابه لذلك الظاهر في الصفحة المقابلة. ويمدّ الرجل الواقع في وسط الصفحة أحد ذراعيه، وقد حطّ صقر عليها، بينما يكون الرجل الثاني في لحظة إطلاق سهم. ويواجه الرجال الأربعة مع خدمهم الأربعة، الموزَّعين على الصفحتين، بعضهم بعضًا. وعند النظر إلى الصفحتين معًا، يبدو وكأن الرجال على وشك الاصطدام ببعضهم البعض بعد لحظات قليلة. وتُؤطَّر كلتا الصفحتين بإطارات مذهَّبة مزخرفة بزخارف نباتية دقيقة وميداليات زرقاء داكنة.
captions.en:
The hunting scene on fol. 2a mirrors the one on fol. 1b. Two men on horses are in the midst of hunting in a similar landscape as the men on the opposite page. The man in the middle of the page has one arm stretched out with a falcon sitting on it. The second man is in the process of shooting an arrow.  
The total of four men and four servants across the two pages are facing each other. If the two pages are looked at together it seems as though the men are only moments away from colliding with one another.  
Both pages are framed by golden borders with intricate floral decoration and deep blue medaillons.

captions.ar: في الصفحة 18a يُقام احتفال داخل حديقة. وفي الوسط يجلس أمير شاب يرتدي ملابس برتقالية زاهية على بساط، محاطًا بأفراد بلاطه وخدم يقدّمون له الطعام والشراب. وفي أسفل المنمنمة يظهر أربعة موسيقيين يعزفون على آلاتهم. يجلس الأمير وحاشيته على مرج أخضر داكن مغطّى بالأزهار. وفي خلفية المشهد تنتصب شجرتا سرو طويلتان إلى جانب شجرتين مزهرتين، تتشابك أغصانهما فيما بينهما. وتبرز الألوان الزاهية للأشجار وأزهارها وملابس أفراد البلاط في تباين واضح مع السماء المذهّبة. وتُؤطَّر المنمنمة بهوامش مزخرفة تضم حيوانات خيالية تتجوّل في مناظر طبيعية مليئة بالأزهار والأشجار، وقد نُفِّذت هذه المشاهد باستخدام اللون الذهبي فقط.
captions.en:
On fol. 18a there is a festivity being held in a garden. In the middle a young prince, wearing bright orange clothes, sits on a carpet. He is surrounded by members of his court and servants offering him food and drinks. At the bottom of the miniature four musicians are playing their instruments.  
The prince and his courtiers are sitting on a dark green meadow that is covered in flowers. In the background of the scene two cypresses stand tall alongside two blooming trees whose branches are meandering between them. The bright colours of the trees, their flowers and the courtiers are contrasted against the golden sky.  
The miniature is framed by marginalia carpeted with fantastical animals roaming a landscape full of flowers and trees. These scenes are painted using only gold.

justifications.en: This type of coin would have been used in the region of Qalát Jabar which experienced Byzantine occupation at the time of Nur al-Din.
justifications.fr: Ce type de pièce de monnaie a dû être utilisé dans la région de Qalat Jabar qui connut l’occupation byzantine au temps de Nour al-Din.
justifications.es: Se podría haber utilizado este tipo de moneda en la región de Qalat Yabar que experimentó la ocupación bizantina en el tiempo de Nur al-Din.

justifications.ar: اسم نور الدين و المنطقة التي حكمها وهي الموصل كلاهما منقوشان على هذه القطعة الزجاجية التي تجعلها معاصرة  للفلس.
justifications.en: Nur al-Din’s name and the region that he ruled, namely Mosul, are both inscribed on this glass fragment, making it contemporary to the fils.
justifications.fr: Le nom de Nour al-Din et la région qu’il gouvernait, appelée Mossoul, sont tous deux inscrits sur ce fragment de verre, ce qui le rend contemporain du fils.
justifications.es: El nombre de Nur al-Din y la región sobre la que gobernó, concretamente Mosul, están inscritos sobre este fragmento de vidrio, siendo así contemporáneo al felús.

captions.ar: تعرض الصفحة 27a اللحظة التي يطل فيها شاب على شابة فيقع في غرامها على الفور، ويحبها حبًا شديدًا. وهذه الحكاية جزء من الفصل الأول من الديوان، تحفة الأحرار. المشهد مُقام في الهواء الطلق؛ يقف البطلان على مرجٍ كثيف الأخضر الداكن بجانب جدول ماء في المقدمة. النصف العلوي من الرسم مُذهب، وقد رُسمت عليه أعواد من العشب الأخضر، ما يوحي بأن هذا الجزء أيضًا يشير إلى المرج. يواجه الشاب والمرأة بعضهما البعض، ويمد الشاب ذراعيه على مصراعيهما، كما لو كان على وشك احتضان الشابة. في المقابل، تمد المرأة ذراعًا واحدة فقط نحوه، بينما يلتف ذراعها الأخرى في عباءتها، ربما كإشارة إلى اهتمام خجول. ميلان جسد الشابة ينعكس في شجرة البرتقال على يمينها، مما يبرز حماستها الظاهرة تجاه الشاب. وبالمثل، قام الفنان بتفصيل فروع الشجرة الطويلة بجانب الشاب لتبدو وكأنها تعكس حركة احتضانه. وبذلك، تم استخدام الطبيعة المحيطة بالمشهد بشكل واعٍ لإنشاء علاقات شكلية مباشرة بين البطلين في هذا المشهد. وقد استُخدمت هذه التقنية بذكاء من قبل الرسامين في جميع أنحاء المخطوطة لتسليط الضوء على الديناميكيات بين شخصيات القصة.
captions.en:
Fol. 27a shows the moment in which a young man, laying his eyes upon a young woman, is smitten, falling instantly in love with her. This anecdote is part of the first chapter of the *divan*, the *Tuhfat al-ahrar*.  
The scene is set outdoors; the two protagonists stand on a lush, dark green meadow next to a stream in the foreground. The upper half of the illustration is gilded and has green blades of grass drawn onto it, which suggests that this part also refers to the meadow. The young man and the woman face each other. The young man has his arms wide open, as if he is about to embrace the young woman. In contrast, the woman extends only one arm towards him while the other one is wrapped in her cloak, possibly as a gesture of shy interest. The inclination of the young woman’s body is echoed in the orange tree on her right, emphasising her apparent enthusiasm for the young man. Likewise, the artist has also articulated the branches of the tall tree next to the young man to seem as though they are mirroring his embrace. The nature surrounding the scene, therefore, has consciously been used to establish direct formal relations between the protagonists of this scene. This technique is cleverly used by the painters throughout the manuscript in order to highlight the dynamics between the story’s characters.

captions.ar: في الصفحة 191a نرى جزءًا من قصة العاشقين المأساويين ليلى ومجنون. لم يدعم والدَي ليلى علاقة ابنتهما بمجنون، ونتيجة لذلك زوجوها لرجل آخر. يقرر مجنون، بعد أن انكسر قلبه، الانتقال إلى الصحراء ليعيش في عزلة. وفي يوم من الأيام، ترسل ليلى رسولًا ليصل برسالة إلى مجنون، ويتفقان على لقاء. وبسبب معارضة أسرة ليلى وزوجها، يضطران إلى الاجتماع سرًا. تجري أحداث لقائهما السري في مكان مفتوح في الهواء الطلق. التركيز الأساسي يقع على العاشقين أثناء لقائهما في المقدمة. يجثو مجنون على الأرض، ويبدو كما لو كان يسجد أمام محبوبته. تعكس ملابسه ومظهره الجسدي الحياة التي عاشها ناسكًا في الصحراء. في المقابل، تظهر ليلى، وهي ترتدي ثيابًا فاخرة، واقفة. تكشف راحتي يديها الممدودتين نحو مجنون للقارئ أنها تسأله عن مظهره المتغير جذريًا. مرة أخرى، تعمل الأشجار والنباتات المحيطة بالشخصيات على إقامة توازٍ شكلي مع أوضاع الشخصيات، مما يبرز الديناميكيات العاطفية للمشهد. يتم فصل البطلين في المقدمة عن الشخصيات الأخرى في اللوحة من خلال تكوين المناظر الطبيعية. ففي حين يجري لقاء ليلى ومجنون أمام خلفية جبلية، يحدث مشهد آخر في الفضاء التصويري وراء هذا التل، حيث تشير الخيام البعيدة إلى وجود مخيم. هنا، ينشغل رجلان في حديث بينهما. وقد تم ترتيب التكوين بشكل متماثل بحيث تحيط خيمة بهذه المجموعة من الشخصيات، مقلدة ترتيب الشخصيات والنباتات في المشهد الرئيسي في المقدمة.
captions.en:
On fol. 191a we see a part of the story of the two star-crossed lovers Layla and Majnun. Layla’s parents did not support their daughter's relationship with Majnun and consequently married her off to another man. A heart-broken Majnun decides to move to the desert to live in solitude. One day Layla sends out a messenger to deliver a letter to Majnun and they both arrange a meeting. Because of Layla’s disapproving family and her husband, they have to meet up in secret.  
The scene of their secret meeting plays out in an outdoor location. The main focus lies on the lovers meeting in the foreground. Majnun is kneeling on the ground, seeming to be prostrating himself in front of his beloved. His clothing and physical appearance reflect the life he has been living as a hermit in the desert. In contrast to Majnun, Layla, richly dressed, is shown standing. Her open palms, raised in Majnun’s direction, reveal to the reader that she is questioning him about his drastically changed appearance. Once again, the trees and plants around the characters establish formal parallels with the figure’s postures emphasizing the emotional dynamics of the scene.  
The protagonists in the foreground are divided from the other characters in the painting through the landscape’s composition. While Layla and Manjun’s meeting takes place against a hilly backdrop, another scene is taking place in the pictorial space beyond this hill where distant tents suggest a camp. Here, two men are absorbed in a conversation. The composition is arranged symmetrically so that a tent flanks this group of figures, mimicking the arrangement of the figures and the vegetation in the main scene in the foreground.

captions.en:
Fol. 33b depicts Katip Celebi's interpretation of the seven climes by Ptolemy. This hints that Katip Celebi had access to Ptolemy's cartographic work *Geographike Hyphegesis* and had probably read it.  
The seven climes are drawn in red and black ink inside a golden circle.

captions.ar: على الصفحة 90b يوجد جزء من مخطط لخريطة الأناضول والبلقان. وقد أُنجز هذا المخطط بشكل تقريبًا بخط اليد باستخدام الحبر العادي، وليس الحبر المخصص للرسم. تم رسم هذه الخريطة على ورقة منفصلة، ثم أُضيفت لاحقًا إلى المخطوطة بعد أن تم ربطها بالفعل. ووفقًا لغوتفريد هاغن، أحد أبرز الخبراء في أعمال كاتب جلبي، تُعد هذه الخريطة واحدة من القليل الذي يمكن نسبه بدرجة كبيرة من اليقين إلى كاتب جلبي نفسه.
captions.en:
On fol. 90b is part of a sketch of a map of Anatolia and the Balkans. The sketch was done rather roughly in writing ink, as opposed to ink made for drawing.  
This map was drawn on a loose piece of paper and was subsequently added to the manuscript after it had already been bound. According to Gottfried Hagen, one of the leading experts on Katip Celebi's work, this map is one of the few that can be attributed with a large degree of certainty to Katip Celebi himself.

captions.en: On fol. 3a, the dedication painting is framed by golden borders around the multi-tiered depiction on a red ground, and can be divided into three horizontal zones. The hunting scene at the top is followed by a larger space encompassing a central square with flanking, towering balconies, and depicted at the bottom is a caravan-like procession. In the central scene, slightly to the left, the ruler, and patron of the manuscript, is emphasised by his height and attributes, such as being in possession of a wine glass and a handkerchief, or *mandil*. He is seated on a low throne furnished with ornate fabrics and cushions, and is wearing elaborate clothes and a high fur-trimmed gilded cap accentuated by a golden halo similar to the other figures surrounding him. Most figures are depicted in three-quarter profile, in keeping with the Seljuq moon-faced ideal of beauty. On the right, a subordinate, potentially a chef, is roasting meat on skewers over an open fire underneath a grate supported by a multi-legged metal base. Behind them, footed trays with fruits, carafes, and flower vases are arranged within the architectural space that is also populated by two sword bearers in the background. The palace architecture with multiple arches and a balcony is made of yellow bricks laid in a pattern and decorated with notched carving. Above in a slim zone representing the balcony, four attendants are wielding shovels or holding up other objects. The white wavy lines at the top of this rectangle space have been interpreted as a cloudy sky or a sun sail, yet the flaking white dots raining down on the workers suggest they are snowflakes. As such, these figures may be shovelling snow from the balcony. The architecture continues laterally to the sides, showing further pairs of attendants in four openings witnessing the central scene: at the top left a lance bearer and a falconer, below a bearded man in conversation with a sword bearer, at the top right a figure holding a duck and a cupbearer, and below two polo players equipped with polo sticks. In the uppermost zone, a hunt for a wild ass and a gazelle is depicted, in which the animals are approached by five riders from either side. They wield bow and arrows as well as falcons, and are followed by a hunting dog, with one falconer on foot visible on the right, behind a grey rock. The dynamic, overlapping forms of the riders highlight the dramatic composition. The rider pursuing the wild ass on a bright yellow horse in the left half of the depiction is visually accentuated by his larger face, the fur-lined princely headdress, a turquoise robe, and the framing green branches of vegetation, potentially representing the ruler. In the lowest zone, the scene is again taking place outdoors but appears calmer, with the procession of a caravan being led by two riders on horses whose gestures suggest conversation with the group of three riders that are approaching from the left. On the right follow four veiled, colourfully dressed female figures with one child, riding on two camels led by a footman. Similar to the workers on the balcony, the riders wear white conical hats.

In the lower half of the page, fol. 3b represents the schematic portraits of the nine doctors of antiquity who are said to have successively produced and further developed theriac. Their names are written vertically to the right of the individual medallion portraits, which are encompassed by thinly-drawn red circles and framed by a red square, and arranged from right to left in three rows. The first doctor is Andromachos (Andruhmakhus) who is depicted in three-quarter profile, with a black beard and blue turban surrounded by a gold halo, as are all of the portraits on the page. He holds an open book with both hands, and appears to be reading from it. The second doctor is Herakleides (Abraqlidis), represented frontally, with a black beard and high light-blue turban. He holds an open book in front of his chest and wears a geometrically patterned robe. The third doctor is Philagrios (Aflaghuras), who is also represented frontally, with a long white beard and small brown cap, holding a closed book to his chest. The fourth doctor, first in the second row, is Proklos (Afruqlus), who is seated in a three-quarter profile with a grey-brown beard and a turquoise turban. In his outstretched right arm, he holds an open book. The fifth doctor is Pythagoras (Buthaghuras), frontally depicted with white hair and beard and a purple turban, holding a red book over his chest. The sixth doctor is Marinos (Marinus) in three-quarter profile, with a grey beard and a blue-golden turban, holding a brown book. The seventh doctor is Andromachos the Younger (Andruhmkhus al-qarib al-'ahd), the first in the third row, who is in three-quarter profile, is depicted with a white beard and hair covered by a round brown cap. He holds a brown book in his arms. The eighth doctor is Magnus (Maghnis), depicted frontally and with a high white turban, but his portrait is not well preserved. The ninth and last doctor is Galenus (Jalinus), who sits in almost full profile, has a white beard and a blue cloak pulled over his high turban. He is holding an open book but looks towards the right.

Fol. 4b illustrates in an oblong rectangular format the story of the physician Andromachus during a horseback ride, who witnesses a boy being bitten by a snake, kills it with a stick, and then cures himself of the effects of its poison by eating laurel fruit. Impressed by this, Andromachus was the first to develop a theriac consisting of four ingredients: laurel fruit, gentian, myrrh, and costus. Andromachus from Crete, personal physician of the Roman Emperor Nero, rides on a yellow, luxuriously bridled horse towards the boy standing in the left half of the picture, who is getting rid of the snake biting his foot with his hand and stick. The white-bearded doctor, dressed in a blue-violet robe covered with fine squiggly folds with golden arm stripes and a green turban, is shown in a side profile. His excitement at this discovery is expressed by his opened mouth and his right hand raised in a speech gesture with an outstretched index finger. The boy, in a three-quarter profile facing the doctor, is shown with slightly bent legs, wearing a knee-length, geometrically patterned, bright red robe with golden arm stripes over long white trousers, as well as a golden cap over his half-length black hair. His beardless, round face is shaped according to the Seljuq ideal of beauty. In-between the two figures, a laurel tree forms the central axis with its red berries and branches positioned symmetrically upwards. Underneath it, a stylised peacock is depicted, and on the far left a heron underneath a tree enlivened by colourful birds. Long-stemmed flowers spring from the lush meadow ground adorned with colourful buds. Golden haloes adorn the heads of the two figures as well as those of the small bluebirds, parakeets, doves, and bulbuls. The sky above is indicated by a two-part blue circle segment of gradient colour.

Fol. 9a depicts in an oblong rectangular format the story of the physician Philagrios and his assistant preparing a theriac. In the right half of the picture, between two fruit trees animated by colourful birds, the white-bearded physician with a turquoise-green turban, green undergarment and blue cloak is seated on a richly gilded and decorated throne with a red backrest. A hoopoe can also be seen flying above him. Philagrios holds a small yellow albarello-type vessel in his outstretched right hand towards his assistant who, standing on the left, seems to be ladling something out of a mighty black cauldron atop a hearth with flickering red flames into a golden bowl he is holding. The assistant, with his round beardless face, corresponds to the Seljuq ideal of beauty. He also wears a red turban, a tight turquoise dress that reaches above his knees, and long white trousers. To his left, a small grey and white cat-like creature climbs up a palm tree. The sky is indicated in blue circular segment shapes. The people and almost all of the birds have gold haloes.

On fol. 10b, the story of Proklos and an assistant making the theriac is illustrated in an oblong rectangular format. The centre of the picture is occupied by a yellow cooker tapering upwards, with golden flames coming out of it, and a similarly shaped black pot in which the assistant, standing on the right, is stirring. With his left hand, he holds his red outer robe with golden arm stripes covering a white long shirt, and moves it away from the heat of the cooker. His round face with a black beard is crowned by a light green turban decorated with gold. His head is surrounded by a gold halo, as is that of the white-haired and white-bearded elderly doctor sitting opposite him with a light blue turban and a geometrically-patterned purple robe. The doctor on the yellow wooden stool points with one outstretched arm to the cooker, while, with the other, he holds up a turquoise-glazed double-handled vessel, likely a medicine container. The scene is completed by a blue-graded segment of sky at the top of the page with a golden full moon in the centre. To the left, the purple trunk of a branched tree with round leaves and red fruit forms the shelter of a grey heron peering out curiously from behind it. The area on the far right is occupied by a magnificent peacock executed in gold, pink and blue tones in front of two trees with yellow fruits populated by haloed green parakeets. Grass with budding flowers as well as long-stemmed plants enliven the blank ground.

At the bottom of fol. 17b, a painting in oblong format illustrates the healing of a leper. Andromachus the Younger relates that he was accustomed to regularly visiting the farmers in a village, possibly called Thurunus, and had his servant bring them food. One day, the servant brought them an earthenware wine jar that had been tightly sealed with a snake inside it. The farm workers made a leper drink from it, who became cured as a result. In the middle of the symmetrical composition sit two bearded men, potentially two doctors, or a doctor and his patient. Nonetheless, the figure on the left has a geometrical pattern on his vermilion robe and wears a blue turban, while the one on the right has a geometrically rosette pattern on his long blue robe, plus a purple turban. The red-clad figure holds a glass goblet of red wine in his right hand, while his other hand grasps the handle of an amphora-like earthenware yellow wine jug that stands on the ground between the two men. The blue-clad man, shown in profile with his mouth eloquently agape, extends his right hand towards the wine jug as if he had just handed it over while his other hand rests on his lap. Above them, likely located behind the pair, is a green pitcher-like vessel and a round three-legged tray with three differently coloured bowls. In the background, cone-shaped trees – perhaps cypresses – are depicted. On the far right and left, two bearded and almost bald farm workers dressed in white loincloths are shown. The one on the left, in profile with his mouth open in speech, is digging in the ground with a long-handled spade, while the one on the right, with a scarf slung around his shoulders, is in three-quarter profile, carrying a tall earthenware jug. Various birds are perched in the branching fruity trees above.

On fol. 18b, a painting in oblong format illustrates the story of Tulunus, the surveyor saved from a snakebite. In another tale, Andromachus the Younger tells of his brother, a royal surveyor, who was awoken by a snake biting into his arm while asleep under a tree. Desperate and expecting to die, he wrote his will, and after drinking water from a large clay jug found nearby, suddenly felt better. Astonished, he examined the bottom of the jar with a twig and found two dead snakes inside, which had apparently bitten each other to death. Andromachus ends the anecdote by saying that his cured brother had given up his profession and had instead devoted his services to being a medical assistant. In the painting, a sleeping man, dressed in a blue robe and a red turban, lies under a tree. His almost suspended, twisted posture seems to capture the moment just before his terrified awakening. A dotted pink-purple snake is coiled around his right arm and bites vigorously into his forearm. Above the man, a huge yellow amphora can be seen, which is a hint to the saving potion. His magnificently saddled and harnessed brown horse stands calmly on the right. Flanking them are two fruit trees enlivened by large coloured birds with small gold haloes symmetrically frame the picture. A few tall flowers and colourful flower buds grow out of the narrow strip of grass, and the painting already shows the title of the next story under the gradient blue-coloured sky segment.

Fol. 19a depicts in an oblong painting the story of the king's favourite slave being poisoned but ultimately saved by a snakebite. In the following story, Andromachus the Younger tells of the king's favourite slave Basthulus (possibly Basileios or Ptolemaios), whom courtiers poisoned with opium out of jealousy and locked him up in a garden house. He was awakened by the bite of a poisonous snake, and when he rapped the door from within the locked house and called for help, gardeners outside heard him and freed him. The poison of the snake had acted as an antidote and saved him from further suffering. The left half of the painting shows a garden with flowers and three fruit trees populated by colourful birds, through which two gardeners dressed only in white loincloths are hurrying with sticks and shovels towards the locked gold-ornamented blue door of the pink brick house. Their animated hand gestures indicate that they hear the pleas of the red-clad man inside the house, who, with arms outstretched towards the door in profile, is knocking and calling for help as a large purple snake bites him in the right leg. While the interior space remains empty, elaborate architectural forms such as a serrated pointed arch and a projecting meandering frieze with alternatingly coloured battlements on the flat roof are shown.

On fol. 20a, five differently-coloured serpents are depicted between single lines of text describing the different serpents. Continuing from a prior page, at the top, the so-called ‘third serpent’ named Al-Ba'yu is shown in light blue with black dots and a lighter blue underside. The following ‘fourth snake’, Al-Miqis or al-Naqqab, is illustrated as a purple grey-spotted snake with a lighter underside as well. The ‘fifth snake’, Al-Mirs al-mu'attash, is brownish-yellow with bronze spots and a white underside. The ‘sixth snake’, Al-Mnunis, is pink with dark red spots and a white underside. The last and ‘seventh snake’, Akhulun, has brownish-pink colouring with red spots and a white underside.

Fol. 22b depicts in an oblong painting a scene of viper hunting. To obtain the poison of the vipers, straw is stuffed into fine, depilated fresh sheep skins. These are formed into human figures and glass eyes are even put into them before they are distributed in large numbers to various places. The vipers, mistaking the puppets for sitting humans, bite into them, expelling some of their poison, and, tired and weakened, become easily impaled by the hunters. In the left half of the painting, framed by two stylised trees, two black-haired, unclothed, cross-legged dolls are sitting, with three pink snakes biting into their shoulder, arm and leg. On the right, a doctor in a long red robe approaches with long golden tongs in his left hand, attempting to catch one of the snakes. He raises his right hand in a seemingly imploring manner and turns his face back towards a beardless youth. The latter, dressed only in a short golden cloak and a blue loincloth, raises his right hand in a speaking gesture towards the doctor, carrying a short stick in his left hand. Between them is a fruit tree, and across the open expanse of sky fly three birds which, like the two people below, have gold haloes.

On fol. 34a, an oblong painting underneath a circular diagram of a theriac formula with gold decorated corner fillings illustrates the story of Galen and his assistant preparing the theriac as shown above. The double image of two physicians, presumably Galen and his assistant, are visible in a kneeling position within a circular frame. The left man in three-quarter profile with a black beard, a blue turban, and a red robe is moving a pestle in a richly decorated gilded mortar with his left hand. The face of his counterpart, dressed in a red turban and green robe, is shown in profile. The latter is holding a decorated golden albarello-type vessel. Three small satchels above them on the central vertical axis may contain medicinal properties.

internal_name: *Kitab al-Tasrif li-man 'ajiza 'an al-ta'lif fi al-tibb* (The arrangement of manifold medical knowledge for one who is not able to compile a book for himself: on surgery and instruments)

captions.ar: في الصفحة 33a نرى ثلاث أدوات جراحية مزخرفة بالحبر الأحمر. وقد وُضعت هذه التصاوير في وسط النص، بحيث تؤدي دور علامات فاصلة بين أقسام النص المختلفة، وفي الوقت نفسه تقدّم تمثيلًا بصريًا لمضمون الأجزاء النصية المجاورة لها. تُصوِّر الأداة العلوية مقصًّا مخصّصًا لجراحة العين، في حين صُمِّمت الأداتان الأخريان لإزالة النواسير من الأنف.
captions.en:
On fol. 33a we see three surgical instruments that are decorated with red ink. The depictions are placed in the middle of the text, doubling as placeholders between the different parts of the text as well as providing a visual representation of the parts of the text they are put next to.  
The upper instrument depicts scissors that are to be used for eye surgery. Meanwhile the two other instruments are designed to remove fistulas from the nose.

captions.ar: تُوضَع الرسمة في الصفحة 37b مباشرة أسفل الثلثين العلويين من النص، ويبدو أن سير النص قد قُطع في هذا الموضع عمدًا، إذ يبدأ فصل جديد عنده. ويزداد التأكيد على هذا الانقطاع من خلال الخط المزخرف الواقع أسفل الرسمة، وهو خط يُستعمل في هذا المخطوط عادةً عند افتتاح الفصول الجديدة. وتُصوِّر الرسمة زوجًا من كماشات الأسنان يشبه إلى حدٍّ كبير الأدوات المستخدمة في الوقت الحاضر. وبفضل الدقة الواضحة في تنفيذ الخطوط المستقيمة والأقواس، يتبيّن أن الرسام استخدم، إلى جانب المسطرة، فرجارًا أيضًا في تنفيذ هذه الرسمة.
captions.en:
The illustration on fol. 37b is placed right underneath the two upper thirds of the text. It seems as though the text was disrupted at this point intentionally as a new chapter starts there. Such a break in the text is further emphasised by the elaborate font underneath the illustration, that throughout this manuscript is typically adopted at the beginning of new chapters.  
The illustration depicts a pair of dental pliers that look fairly similar to the ones that are still in use today. Due to the precise execution of the straight lines and arches, It is apparent that alongside a ruler, a pair of compasses was also utilised for this illustration.

captions.ar: تصوّر الصفحة 42b زوجًا آخر من الملاقط، غير أنّ هذا الزوج صُمّم لإجراء عمليات استئصال اللوزتين وعدة أنواع أخرى من جراحات الحلق. وكما هو الحال مع ملاقط الأسنان في الصفحة 38a، فإن المدهش أنّ هذه الملاقط، ذات الأطراف المائلة، لا تختلف كثيرًا عن تلك المستخدمة في عمليات استئصال اللوزتين في العصر الحديث. وبما أنّ الأداة موضوعة مباشرة فوق عنوان أحد الفصول، فإنها تبدو وكأنها اختيار جمالي لتأكيد العنوان أكثر من كونها تصويرًا منفصلًا. ومن الواضح أنّ هذه الصورة قد نُفّذت جزئيًا بمساعدة أدوات هندسية، إذ رُسمت الخطوط والمقبض العلوي للملاقط بدقة كبيرة. أمّا المقبض السفلي، وبسبب طابعه غير المنتظم، فيبدو أنه قد رُسم يدويًا.
captions.en:
Fol. 42b depicts yet another pair of pliers, however this one is instead designed to perform tonsillectomies and several other kinds of throat surgeries. As is the case with the dental pliers on fol. 38a, amazingly the pliers in question, with their slanted tips, are not too dissimilar from those used in modern day tonsillectomies.  
Given that the instrument is right above the title of a chapter, it makes it look as though it is more of an aesthetic choice to accentuate it rather than a separate illustration.  
Evidently, this particular image must have been partly done with the help of geometric tools, as the lines and the upper handle of the pliers are rendered with great accuracy. However, the lower handle, due to its more uneven character, seems to have been painted freehand.

captions.ar: في الصفحة 58a توجد صورة توضيحية لملقط توليدي مفتوح. وقد ابتكر الزهراوي العديد من الأدوات الخاصة بالولادة، بما في ذلك أجهزة معقّدة يمكن استخدامها كوسيلة مساعدة أثناء العمليات القيصرية. كما كان أول طبيب معروف يصف الحمل البطني في مؤلفاته، إضافة إلى وصف وضعية للولادة عُرفت لاحقًا في مجال التوليد باسم «وضعية فالخر (Walcher position)».
captions.en: On fol. 58a there is an illustration of an opened obstetric forceps. Al-Zahrawi constructed many instruments for childbirth, including intricate devices which could be used as an aid during a caesarean-section. He was also the first known physician to describe an abdominal pregnancy in his works, as well as a birthing position that would be much later on known as the "Walcher position" in the field of obstetrics.

captions.ar: في الصفحة 70b، تُعرض مجموعة مصوَّرة من تسعة أدوات مختلفة تُستخدم في جراحة البطن أو العظام أو الدوالي. وتبدو الأدوات المعروضة على شكل أنواع مختلفة من المشارط والمناشير الجراحية.
captions.en: Fol. 70b serves as a display for an illustrated collection of nine different instruments used for surgery on the abdomen, bones or varicose veins.  The instruments shown seem to be different kinds of scalpels and surgical saws.

captions.ar: تُصوَّر كأس الحجامة في الصفحة 89aمن الجانب. ويزين حافتها زخارف هندسية. ويتصل بالكأس نوع من المقبض، قد يكون مصمماً للمساعدة في تحرير الفراغ أسفل الكأس لإزالتها من جلد المريض.
captions.en: The cupping glass portrayed on fol. 89a is depicted from the side. Along its rim it is decorated with geometrical ornaments. Attached to the cupping glass is a kind of handle, that might be designed to help release the vacuum underneath the glass to remove it from a patient’s skin.

justifications.fr: L’élégant mihrab de la *madrasa* al-Halawiyya d’Alep illustre le travail de l’atelier auquel Nour al-Din confiait la réalisation des *minbar* qu’il commanditait.
justifications.es: Un delicado mihrab de la Madraza de al-Halawiyya en Alepo. Ejemplifica el trabajo del taller en el que Nur al-Din confiaba para los minbars que encargaba.

justifications.ar: قبر صلاح الدين مصنوع من خشب محفور بشكل هندسي مثل المنبر والذي يعتبر العمل المقدس الواقع في المكان المقدس لضريحه.
justifications.en: Saladin’s tomb is made of geometrically carved wood and, like the minbar, is considered a holy work located in the sacred space of his mausoleum.
justifications.fr: La tombe de Saladin, en bois sculpté à motifs géométriques, comme le *minbar*, est considérée comme une œuvre sainte à l’intérieur de l’espace sacré de son mausolée.
justifications.es: La tumba de Saladino está elaborada en madera tallada geométricamente y, como el minbar, fue considerado un trabajo santo situado en un espacio sagrado de su mausoleo.

justifications.ar: الباب الخشبي المحفور بأشكال هندسية في بيمارستان نور الدين هو مثال معاصر للأعمال الخشبية المصنوعة في دمشق.
justifications.en: The geometrically carved wooden door at the Bimaristan Nur al-Din is a contemporary example of woodwork made in Damascus.
justifications.fr: La porte en bois sculpté à motifs géométriques du bimaristan de Nour al-Din est un exemple du travail du produit à Damas à la même époque.
justifications.es: La puerta de madera tallada geométricamente en el bimaristan de Nur al-Din, es un ejemplo contemporáneo del trabajo de madera que se llevaba a cabo en Damasco.

justifications.ar: الاستخدام  الشعائري للمنبر تأسس منذ عهد الرسول و استمر في كل الإمبراطورية الإسلامية كما وجد في هذا المسجد العثماني في إزمير.
justifications.en: The ritual use of the minbar, established since the period of the Prophet, continued throughout the Islamic empire, as found in this Ottoman Mosque in Izmir.
justifications.fr: L’usage rituel du *minbar*, établi depuis la période du Prophète, fut maintenu à travers l’empire islamique, comme on le voit dans cette mosquée ottomane d’Izmir.
justifications.es: El uso ritual del minbar, establecido desde el periodo de El Profeta, continuó durante el imperio islámico, así se evidencia en esta mezquita otomana en Esmirna.

justifications.ar: الوظيفة الشعائرية للمنبر تم احترامها في كل الأراضي الإسلامية و هذا المنبر صنع في الأندلس وقد سلم خلال الحملات الصليبية و تم استرجاعه من قبل المنتصرين.
justifications.en: The ritual function of the minbar was respected all across Islamic lands; this minbar, produced in al-Andalus, was spared during the Crusades and repossessed by the victors.
justifications.fr: La fonction rituelle du *minbar* était respectée à travers tous les pays islamiques ; ce *minbar*, fabriqué en al-Andalus, fut épargné durant les Croisades et récupéré par les vainqueurs.
justifications.es: La función ritual del minbar fue respetada en todas las tierras islámicas; el mimbar, elaborado en Al-Andalus, se salvó durante Las Cruzadas y fue recuperado por los vencedores.

justifications.ar: أمر نور الدين بإنشاء المنبر الأكثر جمالا للمسجد الأقصى في القدس.
justifications.en: Nur al-Din commissioned the construction of his most elaborate minbar to the al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.
justifications.fr: Nour al-Din commandita la construction de son *minbar* le plus élaboré pour la mosquée al-Aqsa à Jérusalem.
justifications.es: Nur al-Din comisionó la construcción del mimbar más elaborado para la mezquita de al-Aqsa en Jerusalén.

captions.en: Fol. 3a displays eight medallions chronologically read from right to left, of which six are filled with paintings while the other two simply include names. On the far right, a medallion with Adam and Eve marks the beginning of the genealogy, and four lines extend from their image to four other medallions. The two figures in three-quarter profile are kneeling before a stream, facing each other within a green landscape with trees and a golden sky: interestingly, Adam and Eve are both fully clad in blue and pink, respectively. Adam has a fiery aureole, while Eve a round halo, denoting a sense of hierarchy between the two. Adam has his hands raised while Eve has hers crossed in front of her body. Above her, a fiery cloud of light extends its rays towards Adam, perhaps signifying the Godly presence. The highest line extending from Adam and Eves’ medallion leads to a painting of their son, 'Abdalharit, clad in light brown and seated in a cross-legged manner in a green landscape. His youthful face is framed by long brown hair. Underneath him, the following medallion reveals the half-figure portrait of Nabi Shith (Seth), a bearded prophet, with a golden-flame halo. At the very bottom, Habil Maqtul (Abel) is shown kneeling on a green ground, inclining his head, and having his right hand slightly raised with his palm turned upwards. His brother Qabil Qatil (Cain), in contrast, is shown to the left of Habils’ medallion, kneeling before a burning altar of sacrifice with his hands raised. His purple robe contrasts with the grey skin colour on his youthful, beardless face, perhaps a reflection of his prior bad deeds. In the left corner, the painting depicts Kayumarth (Gayumars), the first Persian ruler who introduced the furrier craft; hence, he has a lion-skin cape draped over his silver armour. He appears to be in a more dynamic position – potentially running – and holds an attribute, a battle axe, in his right hand.

Following the genealogy on fol. 5a from right to left, multiple medallions containing a portrait or a name are included. The first medallion on the top right features Zahhak Mari, a legendary Persian ruler – indicated by the golden crown with elaborate decoration and luxurious garments in green with a fur-lined red vest – with two serpents extending from his shoulders, as seen here in this image. Following the lines connected to him, on the far left is Faridun Farrukh, another legendary Persian ruler who defeated Zahhak. In contrast to the bearded Zahhak, Faridun is shown as a youthful king with a similarly elaborate crown and the same style of dress, of which only the colours were inverted. Following a different genealogical line on the right, Nuh (Noah) is depicted as the ancestor of the Turks in a half-figure portrait with the arc as his attribute in the background. He is shown as an elderly man with white hair, a turban, and a flaming aureole, having his hands slightly raised as if in conversation, or in referral with his ancestors. On the line connecting Nuh and Faridun, a figure named Bulajas (Abulja Khan, Uljay or Bulja) is depicted. He is the son of Japheth (Yafath), the ancestor of the Oghuz Turks, and wears a fur-trimmed red cap. On the central line extending from Nuh, the portrait of Sam (Shem), Nuh’s son, follows. He has a youthful appearance, clad in a pink robe and wearing a cap with a white band. Sam’s son Arfahshad is depicted next, as a bearded man with a green fur-lined cap and a purple robe. To his left is Sha'ikh (Shabikh), Sam’s great-grandson, who is depicted in a similar manner. To the far left, Hud (Heber) is shown, who was an Arab prophet. As such, a flaming aureole is indicated around his turban.

Fol. 13a depicts eight medallions with portraits, together with multiple name-roundels. At the top, Sevinj Khan, a Turkish ancestor, is shown with a fur-trimmed blue cap and three feathers. To his left, Toghrul Khan, a legendary Turkish ancestor, is depicted wearing a fur-trimmed yellow cap with a hat ornament. Underneath them, in a slightly bigger roundel, Iskandar Zu'l-qarnayn Rumi (Alexander the Great) is shown. He dons a particularly splendid crown, an elaborate multi-layered robe and holds a sabre in his raised left hand. To the left, the prophet Zakariyya (Zacharias), clad in a blue robe and red shawl, is depicted with a flaming halo around his turban. He is facing the figure to the left, Yahya (John the Baptist): this prophet also has a fiery aureole around his turban. Underneath him, Maryam (Mary) is shown with an exposed breast, nursing the baby Jesus, both bearing flaming aureoles. She wears an orange veil, a blue robe, and a pearl necklace, while the child is wrapped in a white cloth. At the bottom, two men are shown: Fihr, the progenitor of the tribe of the Quraysh on the right, and a person named Ghalib in a purple robe, facing the other man.

On fol. 17a, the upper section with blue name-medallions is distinguished from the bottom section which is written in red. At the very top, two Turkish ancestors are portrayed: Qara Bugha Khan is shown wearing a fur-trimmed red cap on the right, while Qumri Khan on the left dons a similarly fur-trimmed blue cap. In the red section, a row of four men in larger medallions are depicted, starting with the Prophet Muhammad on the right. He wears a black turban with a fiery halo around it, and his face is covered by a green veil. His portrait is completely encircled by golden flames extending from the medallion. He is turned towards the men to the left who face the Prophet Muhammad. These three portraits represent Abu Bakr, 'Umar/'Omar, and 'Uthman/'Osman. They are all depicted in a similar manner but with alternating colours of their cap, their garments, and their beard.

Fol. 33a features two large medallions, namely that of Suleyman I Qanuni, who was the Ottoman Sultan from 926 AH / 1520 AD to 974 AH / 1566 AD, who has a grey-white beard, and wears a richly decorated high white turban and an elaborate ermine fur collar over a blue coat. To his left, Selim II is depicted, who was the Ottoman Sultan from 974 AH / 1566 AD to 832 AH / 1574 AD. He has a short brown beard, a similarly decorated high white turban, and a fur-trimmed green cloak.

On fol. 36a, two large medallions portray the two last ruling sultans before the genealogy was completed. On the right, Mehmed IV, Ottoman Sultan from 1058 AH / 1648 AD to 1099 AH / 1687 AD, wears a low white turban decorated with black feathers and a green cap that both match with his luxurious garments. Interestingly, his face is modelled in an expressive and naturalistic manner with a greyish-pink skin colour. The area underneath the eyes is accentuated with deep wrinkles. To the left, Suleyman II, Ottoman Sultan from 1099 AH / 1687 AD to 1102 AH / 1691 AD, also has naturalistically executed features on a pale greyish face. The white turban under a green cap with feather decoration as well as the elaborate garments are similar to those of his predecessor. The detailed execution of these sultans’ facial features may reveal that the painter had direct models at his disposal, or that he wanted to visually comment on the rulers of the immediate past.

justifications.es: En el complejo Süleymaniye se encuentra la tumba del mismísimo Suleyman el Magnífico.

justifications.ar: تحتوي الصفحة الأخيرة من هذا القرآن العثماني أيضًا على طغرة.
justifications.en: The last page of this Ottoman Qur’an also contains a tughra.
justifications.fr: La dernière page de ce coran ottoman comporte aussi un tughra.
justifications.es: La última página de este Corán otomano también contiene una *tugra*.

justifications.ar: طغرة السلطان عثمان الثالث مرسومة على الخشب، وربما كانت تستخدم كنموذج في الديوان الإمبراطوري.
justifications.en: A tughra of Sultan Osman III drawn and painted on wood, probably used as a model in the Imperial Chancery.
justifications.fr: Tughra du sultan Osman III dessiné et peint sur bois, probablement utilisé comme modèle à la chancellerie impériale.
justifications.es: Un tugra del sultán Otman III que se dibujó y pintó sobre madera, probablemente se utilizó como un modelo en la cancillería imperial.

justifications.ar: طقم أدوات كتابة تعود لكاتب أو لمسؤول عثماني، تتضمن  الأدوات اللازمة لقص الورق وتلميعه قبل الكتابة.
justifications.en: A writing set belonging to an Ottoman scribe or official, including all the tools needed to cut and burnish the paper before writing.
justifications.fr: Nécessaire à écriture appartenant à un scribe ou à un fonctionnaire ottoman et comprenant tous les instruments nécessaires pour couper et polir le papier avant d’écrire.
justifications.es: Estos utensilios de escritura eran de un escriba u oficial otomano, incluidas las herramientas necesarias para cortar o pulir papel antes de escribir.

justifications.ar: كانت مثل هذه الطغراءات  للاستخدام الرسمي لقصر توبكابي الذي كان المركز الإداري و الفني للإمبراطورية العثمانية.
justifications.en: Such large tughras were for official use at the Topkapı Palace, which was the administrative and artistic centre of the Ottoman Empire.
justifications.fr: Ces grands *tughra* étaient destinés à l’usage officiel au palais de Topkapı, le centre administratif et artistique de l’Empire ottoman.
justifications.es: Los tugras de este tamaño eran para uso oficial en el palacio Topkapi, el cual era el centro administrativa y artístico del imperio otomano.

justifications.ar: كل من كتاب الصلاة و الطغراء الفريد مستخدم في قصر يحمل رسومات لمكة و المدينة.
justifications.en: Both the prayer book and the master tughra used in the palace bore depictions of Mecca and Medina.
justifications.fr: Aussi bien le livre de prière que le *tughra* principal utilisé au palais portaient des représentations de La Mecque et de Médine.
justifications.es: Tanto el libro de oración como el tugra usados en el palacio incluían representaciones de La Meca y de Medina.

justifications.ar: يبين وجود  الطغراء الارتباط المباشر مع السلطان كما كانت علبة الكتابة هذه لاستخدام السلطان عبد المجيد.
justifications.en: Bearing the tughra indicated direct connection with the sultan – as this writing box was for the use of Sultan Abdülmecid.
justifications.fr: Le fait de porter le *tughra* était un signe de relation avec le sultan – cet écritoire était destiné à l’usage du sultan Abdülmecid.
justifications.es: Portar el tugra era indicio de tener conexión directa con el sultán - esta escribanía era para el uso del sultán Abdülmecid.

justifications.ar: طغراءات  للأحرف الأولى للسلاطين العثمانيين حيث واحد منها هو للسلطان سليمان الكبير و الآخر لعثمان الثالث.
justifications.en: Tughras are the monograms of the Ottoman sultans; one of these was that of Süleyman the Magnificent and the other of Osman III.
justifications.fr: Les *tughra* sont les monogrammes des sultans ottomans ; l’un ce ceux-ci était celui de Soliman le Magnifique, l’autre celui d’Osman III.
justifications.es: Los tugras son los monogramas de los sultanes otomanos; uno de estos era de Süleyman el Magnífico y el otro de Osman III.

justifications.en: This manuscript was preserved in the library of this complex built by Pertevniyal, mother of Sultan Abdülaziz.
justifications.fr: Ce manuscrit était conservé dans la bibliothèque de ce complexe construit par Pertevniyal, la mère du sultan Abdülaziz.
justifications.es: Este manuscrito fue preservado en la librería de este complejo construido por Pertevniyal, madre del sultán Abdülaziz.

justifications.ar: تغطي كلا المخططتين قصص عن النبيين  محمد و موسى.
justifications.en: Both manuscripts cover the stories of Muhammad and Moses.
justifications.fr: Les deux manuscrits racontent les histoires de Muhammad et de Moïse.
justifications.es: Ambos manuscritos abarcan las historias de Muhammad y Moisés.

justifications.ar: صنعت كلا المخطوطتين للسلطان العثماني مراد الثالث.
justifications.en: Both manuscripts were made for the Ottoman Sultan Murad III.
justifications.fr: Les deux manuscrits furent réalisés pour le sultan ottoman Mourad III.
justifications.es: Ambos manuscritos fueron hechos para el sultán otomano Murad III.

justifications.ar: أمر السلطان مراد الثالث بالعديد من الأعمال الفنية بما فيها الكثير من المخطوطات.
justifications.en: Sultan Murad III commissioned many works of art including numerous manuscripts.
justifications.fr: Le sultan Mourad III commandita de nombreuses œuvres d’art, et notamment de nombreux manuscrits.
justifications.es: El sultán Murad III encargó varios trabajos de arte, incluyendo numerosos manuscritos.

justifications.ar: صنعت كلا المخطوطتين للسلطان مراد الثالث و هذه المخطوطة تبين مهرجان الختان لابنه بينما المخطوطة الأخرى هي كتاب عن التاريخ الديني.
justifications.en: Both manuscripts were made for Sultan Murad III. This one depicts the circumcision festival of his son while the other is a religious history book.
justifications.fr: Les deux manuscrits furent réalisés pour le sultan Mourad III. Celui-ci représente la cérémonie de circoncision de son fils tandis que l’autre est un livre d’histoire religieuse.
justifications.es: Ambos manuscritos fueron hechos para el sultán Murad III. Este manuscrito representa la fiesta de la circuncisión de su hijo, mientras que el otro es un libro de historia religiosa.

justifications.ar: لدى الموقع تاريخ طويل مع الاستيطان ولكن تمّ استيطانه بشكل مُكثف خلال الفترة البيزنطية عندما أصبح مقر للأسقفية.
justifications.en: The site has a long history of settlement, but was most intensively settled during the Byzantine period, when it became the seat of the bishopric.
justifications.fr: Le site a derrière lui une longue histoire d’établissement, mais fut plus intensément occupé pendant la période byzantine, lorsqu’il devient le siège de l’évêché.
justifications.es: El emplazamiento tiene una larga historia de asentamientos, pero fue ocupado intensivamente durante el periodo bizantino, cuando se convirtió en la sede del obispado.

justifications.ar: لازالت الكنيسة تُستخدم خلال فترات إسلامية عديدة.
justifications.en: The church continued to be used during several Islamic periods.
justifications.fr: L’église continua à être utilisée pendant les périodes islamiques.
justifications.es: La iglesia continuó utilizándose durante varios periodos islámicos.

justifications.ar: بُني المسجد الجامع بأمر من أسرة بن مروان حيث تحولت مُبكرًا للإسلام كما أنه ربما تمّ استخدام الصليب داخل هذا المبنى خلال الفترة الإسلامية.
justifications.en: The mosque-cathedral was built by the family of Ibn Marwan, early converts to Islam; the cross as a symbol of Christianity may have been used in this building during the Islamic era.
justifications.fr: La mosquée-cathédrale fut construite par la famille d’Ibn Marwan, tôt converti à l’islam ; la croix comme symbole chrétien aurait pu être utilisée dans le monument à la période islamique.
justifications.es: La mezquita-catedral fue construida por la familia de Ibn Marwan, pronto se convierte al Islam, es posible que la cruz como símbolo del Cristianismo se haya utilizado la era islámica.

justifications.ar: يتشابه الصليب اليوناني الموجود بوسط المقبرة الرخامية مع الصليب الأردني.
justifications.en: The Greek cross in the middle of the marble tombstone is similar to the Jordan cross.
justifications.fr: La croix grecque au milieu de la pierre tombale en marbre est semblable à la croix jordanienne.
justifications.es: La cruz griega situada en el medio de la lápida de mármol es similar a la cruz jordana.

justifications.ar: كِلا الصليبين صُنعا من المعدن خلال الفترة الإسلامية.
justifications.en: Both are metal crosses that have been made during the Islamic era.
justifications.fr: Les deux sont des croix en métal fabriquées durant la période islamique.
justifications.es: Es posible que ambas cruces de metal se hayan elaborado durante la era islámica.

justifications.ar: تُظهر العملة المعدنية أشكال لصلبان وكليهما صُنعا خلال الفترة الإسلامية.
justifications.en: The coin shows crosses and both items were made during the Islamic era.
justifications.fr: La pièce montre des croix et les deux objets furent réalisés pendant la période islamique.
justifications.es: La moneda presenta cruces y ambos artículos fueron elaborados durante la era islámica.

justifications.ar: يُظهر الدينار أشكال لصلبان وكليهما صُنعا خلال الفترة الإسلامية.
justifications.en: The dinar shows crosses and both items were made during the Islamic era.
justifications.fr: Le dinar montre des croix et les deux objets furent réalisés pendant la période islamique.
justifications.es: En el dinar se observan cruces y ambos artículos fueron elaborados durante la era islámica.

justifications.ar: تحمل المبخرة رموز مسيحية تشمل الصليب كما تمّ التصنيع خلال الفترة الإسلامية.
justifications.en: The burner bears Christian symbols including a cross and was also made during the Islamic era.
justifications.fr: Le brûleur d’encens porte des symboles chrétiens dont une croix et fut également réalisé pendant la période islamique.
justifications.es: El pebetero presenta símbolos cristianos incluyendo una cruz y fue elaborado también durante la era islámica

internal_name: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim b. Muhammad al-Farisi al-Istakhri, *Kitab Suwar al-Aqalim* (Book of Images of the Lands)

captions.en: Fol. 1b includes an initial ornamental heading panel (*‘unwan/sarlauh*) with golden medallions and palmette shapes before a dark blue background filled with small brightly coloured floral scrolls. The central golden panel is inscribed in white with the title of the text. The brightly coloured floral scroll before a golden background extends playfully into the text block underneath, framing the lines of text at the top and at the bottom.

Fol. 2b includes a full-page illustration of the world map, framed at the top and bottom by title panels that are filled with ogival medallions that incorporate large headings in *thuluth* script, and are surrounded by a dense network of floral patterns. The square panel between them incorporates a roundel with the world map in circular form; the spandrels are filled with golden flowers before a white background. The caption in the panel above reads “*Surat al-Ard,*” or “picture of the world.” Al-Istakhri begins his treatise with a stylized map of the world preceding all regional maps. Its main purpose was to schematically indicate the position of the regions and their relationship to each other as well as to enable the reader to correctly classify the various regional maps. The circular map shows all known continents at the time, and the outside ring represents the encircling sea, as medieval scholars assumed that the other hemisphere was completely covered with water. The land mass is divided into geometric shapes with toponyms identifying the respective designated places, with Europe shown on the right. The three prominent islands in the Mediterranean Sea are likely Cyprus, Crete and Sicily. Africa is divided at the top by the Nile, which is shown as a straight channel extending upwards. Below the Nile, Egypt (*Misr*) and Syria (*Sham*) are indicated, and towards the left, the Indian Ocean opens into the encircling sea. The three circles within the map could be three small islands strategically located in the Persian Gulf. In the bottom left, the region of Khorasan is indicated, and towards the bottom centre, the Caspian Sea, the largest lake on earth, is shown in a keyhole-like shape. The high degree of abstraction of the stylised straight and curved lines in gold emphasises that there was no attempt to reproduce on any actual scale. Possibly, this type of representation served as an aid to memory. Moreover, the map is clearly readable and thus easily reproducible by copyists.

Fol. 9a features the regional map of Arabia. The full-page illustration includes colourful circles with inscribed toponyms possibly designating regions or large cities. These are arranged in a particular formation; for example, in the top right corner, the country of Oman is indicated as a light pink circle while Sana’a, the largest city of Yemen, is represented as a green circle slightly to the left. On the top right, the rectangular block reads “*Ab-e Zamzam*”, which references the so-called Zamzam Well in the courtyard of the *Masjid al-Haram* in Mecca. In-between these circles, trees, flowery shrubs and mountain formations with identification markers are incorporated. In the bottom left corner, a man with a golden fiery aureole appears to be involved in some form of manual work.

Fol. 102b features the Caspian Sea as a large roundel with wave patterns before a blue background. The depicted river, which has been designated as the “*Rud-e Atil*”, the Volga, extends to the bottom left corner of the full-page illustration. It is Europe’s longest river, which flows into the Caspian Sea. Next to it, an orange circle with the same name as the river likely denotes the capital city of historical Khazaria. Other colourful circles with added toponyms also designate regions or large cities and in-between them are flowery shrubs arranged in a decorative manner. On the bottom left, a man on a horse is depicted with a fiery aureole. The inscription identifies him as “Hazrat Khizir ‘Ali al-Eslam”, potentially a prophet or guide of mystical journeys. His right hand was either not finished or is deliberately missing. Above his head, the light pink circle represents Abaskun, a medieval port and trading hub on the Volga trade route.

internal_name: Abu Mansur Muwaffaq ibn 'Ali al-Harawi, *Kitab al-Abniya 'an haqa'iq ad-adwiya* ('The Book of Fundamentals on the True Nature of Remedies')

captions.en: On fol. 1r – the first page of the manuscript – four lines of text in varying sizes of calligraphic angular Persian *kufic* script can be seen in an elegant ductus, which functions as the sole form of ornamentation. The monumental black script designates the title in the first line and the dedication of the copy at the bottom. The word in largest letters, which translates to ‘book’ (*kitab*) located at the top, is written in a decorative manner: the first letter (*kaaf*) is elongated to make the word extend over the whole line, while the letter *alef* vertically reaches up to the very top. The next one in the hierarchy of size is the dedicatory note at the bottom, which appears to be more important than the actual title or the author’s name. The latter is enclosed between the monumental black calligraphy, presented in the smallest line of script, which, however, is written in red and thus visually distinguished, as usually the most important words are written in this colour. Turkish glosses are added in the margin at the top of the page.

internal_name: Abu Yahya Zakariyya' ibn Muhammad al-Qazwini, *'Aga'ib al-makhluqat wa-ghara'ib al-maujudat* ('The Wonders of Creation and the Marvels of Creation')

captions.en: Fol. 1b features an initial ornamental field (*'unwan/sarlauh*) in Ottoman-Turkish styled painting. A geometrically decorated band of red with black detail frames the ornamental field on the sides and creates a base for the title cartouche that was left empty. The half-medallion or pediment on top of the cartouche incorporates blue and gold floral arabesques with flowers in an interlaced manner, extending to the top through vertical floral motifs in blue.

On fol. 18b, an illustration of Saturn reveals a figure clad in red and green with six flatly drawn arms presenting various attributes: a spear, a rod, a scourge and a rat. Interestingly, the head is rendered in an undefined black shape. The figure is situated on the lower half of the page, drawn without any regard for the border of the text block. Immediately preceding the illustration, a group of words written in red include the Arabic name of Saturn. Below the scourge, written in the same tone of red over the frame, is an Arabic word potentially referring to judgement.

Fol. 28a shows two signs of the zodiac, Gemini and Cancer, in separate illustrations. On the upper half of the page, following a three-line paragraph, the painting of Gemini is inscribed within the text border and flanked by brightly coloured vines with flowers in red, ochre, blue, and green. The zodiac sign is rendered as two figures in red and ochre with one eye each and connected by an embrace-like posture. The following paragraph opens with a red-coloured group of words including the word for Cancer, referring straight away to the painting underneath, which extends into the margins. Long vines with coloured flowers in a similar colour scheme to the drawing above surround the abstracted yet recognisable drawing of a crab in black colour.

On fol. 48b, a circular diagram extending over half of the page identifies the beginnings of the months. The corresponding words in the following paragraphs are highlighted in red. In contrast to the other paintings, this diagram is drawn in a more exact and diligent manner. It is likely that it was made by the scribe himself, rather than by the painters responsible for the illustrations.

Fol. 79b features a large pink bird with orange features between two paragraphs within the text block. The painting recounts the ancient legend of a miraculous bird that rescued a man from Isfahan, who was abandoned on a desert island. In an almost comic manner, the man, clad in green, orange, and ochre, is holding onto the bird’s feet and dangling at a strange angle as if he will fall off into the margin. Despite the simple and less precise drawing style, the painter managed to convey a certain drama with the bird in mid-flight and the man’s large bulging eyes and long moustache as he clings onto the bird’s claws.

The upper half of fol. 98b depicts the four bearers of the Throne of Heaven from the vision of Ezekiel, or symbols representing the four evangelists. An anthropomorphic figure with wings occupies the top right space of the page, followed by a bull in the left-hand corner. Below the bull, a drawing of an animal referencing an eagle is visible, and next to it, a rather abstractly drawn lion. The pair of figures at the top and bottom face each other yet seem to serve a purely emblematic purpose. Here, the text border is again disregarded, with the large figures drawn over it, unapologetically extending into the margins.

Fol. 115b presents the only full-page illustration of Shabdiz, a pleasure palace near Bisotun, named after the horse of Khusrau II (r. 590-628 AD). The architectural structure is only shown in preliminary outlines, appearing to be unfinished. Within it, on the top, a figure with a crown is seated cross-legged in the centre, likely Khusrau himself. He is flanked by male figures with turbans and hats, probably representing his court or retinue. On the column-like structure in the outer margin, a veiled lady’s bust is depicted on the same level. Another figure at the bottom of the column, perhaps standing in a doorway, is gesturing to the depiction on the left: the only space with a fully coloured background filled with floral vines and white-orange flowers extending from a flat bowl at the bottom. At the top of the drawing, underneath a medallion-shaped arch, Khusrau is depicted again on horseback – likely on his horse Shabdiz – with a crown and either his insignia or hunting gear. He is surrounded by three attendants who are turning towards him. The grey background suggests that this depiction may be a mural, yet the fact that one figure’s feet are drawn outside this coloured area makes this fact more ambiguous. However, the hypothesis was put forward that the architectural structure and figures outside this mural-like painting were added by a different painter.

On fol. 130a, a nilometer structure is shown on a large scale within the text block, likely presenting a temple architecture of different compartments, all of which are brightly coloured. It is a structure that measures the water level of the Nile during flood season, and therefore was an important aspect of Egyptian agriculture. One type of nilometer, which is shown here in the lower part of the illustration, is a column with horizontal lines, which is likely a subterranean chamber underneath a burning fire and a lamp shown above. A figure is standing to the right, next to another contraption, likely a priest monitoring the changing water level.
